report:
The explicit-family theorem is supported by the supplied proof, but it does not resolve the authoritative problem. It proves all-obstacle equality for specially constructed potentials on positive Hermitian backgrounds. It supplies neither the universal implication for arbitrary admissible theta and u nor an obstacle with unequal envelopes. The manuscript expressly acknowledges this limitation; I found no concrete mathematical defect warranting FAIL.

The construction checks out. For s=log R², the radial profile has positive tangential and radial Hessian eigenvalues q′(s)/R² and q″(s)/R². The flattened profiles remain convex increasing, decrease as A increases, agree with the original profile on the cutoff transition for sufficiently large A, and converge in L¹. Their centre values tend to −∞. Scaling the two finite transition bounds simultaneously gives the claimed common delta_j. Summability of the L¹ norms prevents either countable limit from being identically −∞. Adding a fixed local quadratic makes the partial sums plurisubharmonic, so their actual decreasing limits are canonical and retain h+Du,h+Dw≥3h/4. Each prescribed point is an actual pole; density therefore gives unboundedness below on every nonempty open set.

The stronger-minorant argument is valid: beta′>beta makes M_b finite, and the finite-sum inequalities pass to w≤bu+M_bS, including common poles. Consequently tw≼u for every 0<t≤1. The genuine h-psh function v=w−M_bS satisfies b⁻¹v≤u, establishing the stated relative-envelope membership directly from the original definition.

The exponential-integrability proof also works for every real positive scale. Weighted Jensen with the missing tail weight assigned exponent zero gives uniformly bounded integrals. After radial substitution, the controlling exponent is −nx+sS(1+x)^sigma, which is integrable for both sigma=beta and sigma=beta′. Monotone convergence gives the asserted global integrability. Boundedness of holomorphic germs on smaller balls then proves I(su)=O_X in the task’s exact convention.

The envelope lemma preserves the exact nonclosed background. Convolution introduces only a uniformly vanishing error in the lower Hessian bound; the smooth convex maximum preserves that bound, and L¹ convergence removes the error. A fixed quadratic supplies canonical finite maxima. Choquet selection followed by dominated L¹ convergence between a genuine anchor and F passes the exact current inequality to the regularized supremum. Continuity of F preserves the obstacle inequality. Thus W=P_h(F) is genuine and bounded. Trivial multiplier ideals make the ideal envelope exactly W. Each A_t=(1−t)W+tw−t||F||∞ is genuine, lies below F, and satisfies A_t≼u. Hence A_t≤O≤W. On the full-measure finite locus of w, A_t tends to W; canonical uniqueness upgrades O=W almost everywhere to equality everywhere, including poles. For F=0, W=0.

The cited local results and their relevant proof contexts were checked in [Demailly’s 2012 manuscript](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), including Choquet’s lemma. Their applications require no local potential for h and no Monge–Ampère theorem. The conditional applicability to a given background with exceptional mass behaviour does not establish such a geometry or settle arbitrary u.

One harmless wording correction is needed in supporting note 1: the flattened radial function is constant near the coordinate centre; q_A(s) is constant for s≤−2A, not near s=0. The manuscript’s formulas already state the correct behaviour. The missing universal argument requires substantial new work.

passages.statement: On an open subset Ω of C^n, the pointwise limit of a decreasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions is plurisubharmonic, possibly identically −∞ on a component (Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.4).
passages.quote: the limit u = lim uk is plurisubharmonic on Ω.

passages.statement: The pointwise maximum of finitely many plurisubharmonic functions on an open subset Ω of C^n is plurisubharmonic, with value −∞ at a common pole (Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.6).

For a nonempty, locally uniformly bounded-above family of plurisubharmonic functions on an open subset Ω of C^n, the regularized supremum is plurisubharmonic and equals the pointwise supremum almost everywhere (Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.7).

A nonempty, locally uniformly bounded-above family of upper semicontinuous functions with values in [−∞,+∞) on an open Euclidean domain has a countable subfamily with the same regularized supremum (Demailly, Chapter I, Lemma 4.23).

Locally integrable plurisubharmonic functions have positive distributional complex Hessians. Conversely, a real distribution on an open subset Ω of C^n whose complex Hessian in every constant complex direction is a positive measure has a unique locally integrable plurisubharmonic representative (Demailly, Chapter I, Theorem 5.8).
